A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same selective Jacobi decoding work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original TarFlow experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and AFHQ, including inference comparisons, dependency analyses, convergence measurements, and stopping-threshold ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MAF experiments, initialization tests, reconstruction measurements, resource analyses, and comparisons with other generative models.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the TarFlow procedure retain the same Jacobi updates, stopping rule, and sequential first layer. Appendix E.3 extends the layer-selection policy for MLP-based MAF: without KV caching, Jacobi decoding is applied to every layer. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image generation on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and AFHQ. v2 adds binary MNIST generation and Boltzmann-distribution approximation for a high-temperature 2D Ising model, substantially extending coverage beyond the original image domains. It also evaluates image reconstruction on the retained datasets.

E2.justification: The sequential and uniform Jacobi baselines remain in Table 1. v2 adds an evaluated CIFAR-10 comparison with the baseline labeled FastGAN and DDIM at 20 steps in Appendix E.5/Table A6, extending comparisons from decoding alternatives to distinct generative-model families.

E3.justification: The main TarFlow protocol remains unchanged. New protocols include eight-layer MAF experiments, 3,000 reverse-KL training epochs and 100,000 evaluation samples for Ising, 20-step DDIM, round-trip reconstruction MSE, and memory measurement at batch size 16. The dependency analysis also adds L2 distance. Newly disclosed TarFlow configurations do not establish changes to its existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds zero/Gaussian/previous-layer initialization ablations, quantitative dependency analyses at additional masking offsets, reconstruction-error tests, and per-layer iteration, runtime, and memory analyses. These substantially extend robustness and mechanism validation. The original full convergence plots are retained as Figure A2 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report maximum deviations across three CIFAR runs in Table 1 and average TarFlow timing over ten runs. v2 introduces no new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure; its additional results principally use point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged. v2 nevertheless adds substantial results: 15.7× Ising and 18.4× binary-MNIST acceleration, reconstruction MSEs of 0.00636/0.00313/0.00122, memory usage of 5.2 versus 7.8 GB, and cross-model and runtime-breakdown results. Figure 1 also changes its reported dependency curves and replaces its CIFAR-10 panel with CIFAR-100.

T1.justification: The convergence propositions and proof strategies are retained. v2 replaces the proof's C1-diffeomorphism assumption with continuous differentiability and corrects inconsistent K-versus-L finite-convergence statements. Appendix D adds an argument that both implementations have O(L²) memory complexity. These are localized mathematical corrections and additions.

C1.justification: The central claims remain layer-dependent redundancy, training-free selective Jacobi acceleration, superlinear and finite convergence, and up to 4.7× acceleration with little generation-quality loss. The new experiments support the existing generality claim. The added 'discrete' terminology clarifies the finite-cascade setting already studied.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning initialization insensitivity, architecture-dependent layer selection, memory savings from avoiding KV storage, reconstruction consistency, and GAN/diffusion tradeoffs. The original undertraining and training-optimization limitations remain. Its new claim of preserving 'strict bijective consistency' is stronger than the reported nonzero reconstruction errors directly establish.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 supplies a project-code URL. Table A2 newly documents batch sizes, sequence lengths, and AFHQ architecture alongside retained CIFAR settings. The appendices also identify the nflows implementation, MAF training/evaluation settings, and the diffusion checkpoint, substantially expanding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain largely unchanged. v2 adds Zhong et al. (2020) for its GAN comparison and contextualizes results against GANs and diffusion models. TarFlow's updated publication information and the switch to author-year citations do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title, author information, prose, and terminology, including replacing image-specific 'patches' with 'sub-variables'. It rewrites the preliminaries, folds experimental settings into Section 4, and regroups appendices with a notation guide. The overall motivation-method-evaluation narrative and most section sequencing remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different publication layout, redraws Figure 1 with dual metrics, adds an initialization chart, six appendix tables, and new diagnostic and reconstruction figures. The full original Figure 4 moves to Figure A2 while the main text shows two panels; original Figures 6–7 become Figures A7–A8. These changes substantially reorganize visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was confined to TarFlow and lacked direct reconstruction and resource diagnostics. v2 addresses these gaps with another architecture, a non-image sampling task, initialization and reconstruction tests, and detailed inference profiling and reproducibility information. These additions substantially strengthen validation of generality and practical behavior while retaining the original main results. The reconstruction appendix overstates exact bijective preservation, but that qualification does not outweigh the broader evidential improvements.
